(a) Extension.—Notwithstanding section 2002 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (division B of Public Law 111–84; 123 Stat. 2627), the authorization set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2401(a) of that Act (123 Stat. 2640), shall remain in effect until October 1, 2013, or the date of the enactment of an Act authorizing funds for military construction for fiscal year 2014, whichever is later. 
    (b) Table.—The table referred to in subsection (a) is as follows:Extension of 2010 Project Authorization

fable.w: This section only extends the duration of a prior military construction project authorization for a Pentagon electrical upgrade. It involves no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. The reference to a future Act of Congress is purely an internal federal trigger and not participation.
fable.s: the authorization set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2401(a) of that Act (123 Stat. 2640), shall remain in effect until October 1, 2013

qwen_block.w: This section merely extends the authorization for a specific military construction project (Pentagon electrical upgrade). It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The text deals solely with internal federal funding authorizations and timelines.
qwen_block.s: the authorization set forth in the table in subsection (b)... shall remain in effect until October 1, 2013

opus.w: This section only extends the deadline on an existing military construction authorization for a Pentagon electrical upgrade. No one outside the federal government is consulted or given any role in a federal decision. The word "Virginia" in the table's "State" column marks the project's location; it does not bring the state into the decision.
opus.s: the authorization set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2401(a) of that Act (123 Stat. 2640), shall remain in effect until October 1, 2013
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The table has a "State" column, and the section concerns a federal construction decision, so one might read it as involving a state. That fails. "Virginia" only says where the Pentagon project is. No state, tribe, expert or member of the public is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue. The section just extends a funding authorization, which Congress does inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely extends the authorization for funding a specific military construction project (Pentagon electrical upgrade). It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The text is purely administrative regarding budget authority.
qwen_chat.s: The authorization set forth in the table in subsection (b)... shall remain in effect until October 1, 2013...
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the project is for the Pentagon (a federal facility), any decision-making process inherently involves federal actors only, so it's "No". However, the text itself does not describe any decision-making process, consultation, or participation mechanism at all. It is purely an appropriation/authorization extension. The lack of any mention of outside parties makes the "No" label robust, but the reasoning must focus on the absence of participation mechanisms, not just the identity of the beneficiary.
